title: Runtime: add profile pack loader + schema validation; seed H100/L40S profiles (flagged)
author: Ethan Park
body:
Title: Runtime: add profile pack loader + schema validation; seed H100/L40S profiles (flagged)

Context
We’re starting the “hardware tuning profiles pack” work (ENG-4922). This PR adds the first end-to-end skeleton:
- A runtime-visible profile pack artifact (YAML) that can be loaded at startup
- Strict schema validation + helpful errors
- Initial profile definitions for H100 and L40S, but gated behind a feature flag (default OFF)

This is intentionally conservative: the pack can be loaded and validated without changing any scheduling/kernel defaults unless enabled.

What’s in this PR
1) Profile pack loader
- New module: runtime/profile_pack/*
- Loads a single YAML document via:
  (a) --profile-pack-path flag
  (b) RUNTIME_PROFILE_PACK_PATH env var
  (c) default search path: /etc/redwood/profile-pack.yaml (when present)
- Supports hot-reload = NOT in scope. Load-once at process start.

2) Schema + validation
- New schema version: v1alpha1
- Validation runs before runtime initialization completes; failures are fatal only when profile pack is enabled.
- Validates:
  - required top-level fields (apiVersion, kind, metadata, profiles)
  - unique profile_id
  - known enums (sku, workload_bucket, scheduler_mode)
  - numeric ranges (concurrency caps, batch token limits, kv_cache headroom)
  - “safe defaults” constraints (e.g., disallow kv_cache_target_utilization > 0.92 unless allow_unsafe_overrides: true)

3) Feature flag / kill switch
- Flag: runtime.profile_pack.enabled (default: false)
- When disabled:
  - loader may still parse/validate in “warn-only” mode to surface errors without impacting traffic
  - no knob values are applied; runtime uses existing defaults
- When enabled:
  - selected profile knobs override runtime defaults (selection logic is minimal here; full selection rules will land in follow-up PRs)

4) Seed profiles (flagged)
- Adds profile-pack/examples/profile-pack.v1alpha1.yaml with:
  - H100 baseline profile: h100-sxm-default-v1
  - L40S baseline profile: l40s-default-v1
- These are placeholder defaults aligned with today’s safe operating envelope (not aggressive throughput tuning yet).

5) Tests
- Unit tests for:
  - YAML parsing and schema validation
  - validation error messages (golden snapshots)
  - feature flag semantics (apply vs no-op)

Non-goals / explicitly deferred
- Deterministic selection rules by (sku, driver, cuda, model family, workload bucket). That is ENG-4923.
- Compatibility gate by driver/CUDA and MIG/no-MIG. Partial hooks are present, but policy is stubbed.
- Any production default change. This is gated.

Operational notes
- When enabled, runtime logs a one-line summary at startup:
  - profile_pack_version, active_profile_id (if resolved), and pack path
- For now, active profile resolution is “first matching sku” if runtime detects a known SKU. If multiple match, we error (when enabled) to avoid nondeterminism.

Files / areas changed (high level)
- runtime/profile_pack/loader.ts: load pack from path/env/default
- runtime/profile_pack/schema_v1alpha1.ts: schema + validators
- runtime/profile_pack/apply.ts: apply validated knob set to runtime config (gated)
- runtime/config/flags.ts: adds runtime.profile_pack.enabled and profile pack path flag
- profile-pack/examples/profile-pack.v1alpha1.yaml: seed definitions for H100/L40S
- runtime/profile_pack/__tests__/*: validation + flag semantics

Illustrative snippet (schema)
apiVersion: redwood.ai/runtime-profile-pack/v1alpha1
kind: RuntimeProfilePack
metadata:
  pack_version: "0.1.0"
profiles:
  - profile_id: "h100-sxm-default-v1"
    sku: "H100"
    knobs:
      scheduler:
        mode: "mixed_prefill_decode"
        max_inflight_requests: 96
      batching:
        max_prefill_tokens_per_batch: 8192
      kv_cache:
        target_utilization: 0.88

CI
- runtime-unit-tests: pass
- runtime-lint: pass
- config-golden-tests: pass

Follow-ups
- ENG-4923: selection rules + override precedence
- ENG-4931: add profile_id tag to metrics (this PR only logs)
- ENG-4927: L40S constraints + tuned defaults after baseline benchmarks

Requested review focus
- Schema fields and validation approach (Anika)
- Safety/rollout semantics (Sean)
- Runtime initialization ordering / config layering (Noah)

Rollout plan
- Land behind runtime.profile_pack.enabled = false
- Enable in dev/staging once selection rules land

Co-authored-by: Omar El-Sayed <omar@redwood.ai>
commits: runtime/profile-pack: add YAML loader + default search paths
runtime/config: add profile_pack.enabled feature flag and pack path flag
profile-pack: add example pack with initial H100/L40S profiles
tests: add golden validation errors + flag semantics coverage
review_conversation:
Noah Patel: Can we avoid fataling the process on schema errors while flag is off? I’d prefer we only hard-fail when enabled, but still surface errors loudly.
Ethan Park (author): Yep — updated to validate in warn-only mode when runtime.profile_pack.enabled=false. When enabled, we fail fast with a single aggregated error message including profile_id context.

Anika Gupta: Schema: please enforce unique profile_id and forbid unknown fields under knobs to avoid silent typos.
Ethan Park (author): Added unique profile_id check + strict decoding for knobs (unknown fields produce validation errors). Updated golden tests.

Hiro Tanaka: The seed H100 profile includes scheduler.mode=mixed_prefill_decode. Is that actually the current default? I don’t want this pack to imply a behavior change.
Ethan Park (author): Good call. With flag OFF, no behavior change. With flag ON, this will set it — but we’re not enabling. I added a comment in the example pack: “placeholder; does not ship enabled by default”.

Sofia Ivanova: Can we rename max_inflight_requests to match existing config naming? Otherwise apply() is going to create a second concept.
Ethan Park (author): Renamed to scheduler.queue_max_inflight to mirror runtime config. Updated schema + example + apply mapping.

Sean Gallagher: Please add an explicit kill-switch semantics note in the PR description and ensure the pack path isn’t required (avoid crash loops if file missing).
Ethan Park (author): Added note. If pack file missing: warn when flag OFF; error only when flag ON and path is explicitly set. Default search path missing is treated as “no pack”.

Sahana Iyer: Tests look good. One request: add a small test for duplicate profile match resulting in a deterministic error.
Ethan Park (author): Added test: errors when >1 profile matches detected SKU (only when enabled).
